pages.quiz:
HOME SCIENCE MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Special Treatment in Laundry Work? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.

12. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Meals for Special Occasions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Convenience Foods and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Pastry Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Yeast Products and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

2. C — Ice melting to water

3. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.

6. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

9. D — 100 °C

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.

12. B — Producers

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Meals for Special Occasions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pastry Making; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Yeast Products; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
